articleHeadline: Pretomanid resistance found in 4.5% of tuberculosis isolates in China
articleSummary: China-wide study of 335 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from drug-resistance surveillance regions in patients with no prior pretomanid exposure found a baseline pretomanid resistance rate of 4.5% (15/335). The dataset is predominantly lineage 2 (77.9%), and the 99th percentile MIC applies to both lineage 2 and lineage 4 in China. The findings indicate phenotypic resistance can exist without known mutations, highlighting limitations of molecular assays and providing MIC-distribution data to support ECOFFs and clinical breakpoints for broth microdilution in China. For interpretation, isolates with MIC ≥0.5 mg/L may be considered probably resistant.

articleSummary: Chandipura virus, a neurotropic vesiculovirus of Rhabdoviridae, was first isolated in Chandipura, Maharashtra, India (1965). The disease primarily affects children under 15, starting with fever and progressing to convulsions, coma or death. Notable outbreaks include 2003 Andhra Pradesh and later events in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha and Bihar; a Gujarat cluster involved 148 cases with 51 laboratory-confirmed infections. BBB maturation may underlie age differences.

However the TB burden remains heavy, especially among children, people living with HIV, the malnourished, residents of remote areas, and those in crowded settings. Key obstacles are insufficient diagnostic equipment, uneven geographic distribution, maintenance problems, and frequent stockouts of antituberculosis medicines. Some clinics lack power or cartridges; patients travel long distances for molecular testing. Delays in diagnosis worsen disease, increase costs and mortality, and prolong transmission.
